lyrics:
[Intro: bright trumpet fanfare, male hype voice, crowd whoops]
Ladies up, gentlemen too
This one is for the ones who thought they forgot
Dale

[Verse 1: male voice, half rapped, congas and bass]
I never really planned on getting up tonight
My knees filed a complaint and my back's not right
But she walked to the floor like the tide comes in
And the room rearranged itself around her spin

[Pre-Chorus: female lead, breathy, guitar plucks]
Oh, I haven't done this in so long
But the body keeps the song

[Chorus: female lead, full band, trumpets answer]
My feet know the way (como?)
My feet know the way
I can't remember names but I remember this sway
Mira, the head forgets, the heart delays
But my feet, my feet know the way

[Verse 2: female lead, playful, percussion busy]
Abuela in the kitchen with the radio high
Taught me one-two-three before I learned to tie
My shoes, and now the years are on my hips
But the count comes back like a word to my lips

[Pre-Chorus: female lead, breathy, guitar plucks]
Oh, I haven't done this in so long
But the body keeps the song

[Chorus: female lead, full band, trumpets answer]
My feet know the way (como?)
My feet know the way
I can't remember names but I remember this sway
Mira, the head forgets, the heart delays
But my feet, my feet know the way

[Bridge: Spanish, drums and handclaps only, crowd joins]
Baila, que la vida es corta
Baila, que nadie nos mira
Y si nos miran, no importa
Baila, baila, mi vida

[Verse 3: male voice, hype, trumpets stab]
From the east side to the islands, from the valley to the bay
For my mother and her sisters and the ones who went away
Put your hand up if your people ever cleared a kitchen floor
One more time for mi gente, then we do it all once more

[Final Chorus: both voices, trumpets on top, whistles]
My feet know the way (como?)
My feet know the way
I can't remember names but I remember this sway
Mira, the head forgets, the heart delays
But my feet, my feet know the way

[Outro: trumpet fanfare, laughter, last drum hit]
Otra vez
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 100 BPM, 4/4, B-flat minor. A rolling Latin-pop groove that mixes reggaeton's kick pattern with cumbia and salsa percussion. Warm, loud and physical.

VOICE: A female lead with a flexible, slightly husky voice, quick flips into head voice and a rapid vibrato on held notes. A male voice who half raps the first verse, narrates and shouts encouragement between her lines. A party crowd singing the bridge.

INSTRUMENTS: A bright trumpet section playing a fanfare that opens the song and answers the chorus. Congas, timbales, guiro and cowbell. A reggaeton-style kick and snare pattern. Round, bouncing bass. Nylon-string guitar plucks. Accordion-like synth in the verses. Handclaps and whistles.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, trumpet fanfare and the hype voice. 0:12 Verse 1, male voice. 0:31 Pre-chorus, female lead. 0:41 Chorus 1. 1:05 Verse 2, female lead. 1:24 Pre-chorus. 1:34 Chorus 2. 1:58 Bridge in Spanish over drums and claps, the crowd joining line by line. 2:22 Verse 3, the dedications. 2:41 Final chorus with both voices and the trumpets on top. 3:10 Outro, the fanfare again, laughter, a final drum hit at 3:30.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2000s global pop: punchy low end, bright horns, percussion spread wide, vocals close and lively with the ad-libs left in.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The trumpet fanfare in the first two seconds.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The dancers are not twenty-two. Their knees complain, they learned the steps from a grandmother, and the joy is in finding it all still there. The dedication is to families and kitchens, not to one city.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Reluctance, surprise, memory, shared joy.
